adjudication_label: batch_18:Selective chemical dissolution and surface treatment effects
canonical_question: Will the 'aqua regia' treatment affect the surface composition of the Mo-rich phases differently than the Ni-rich matrix?

question_variants.question: Will the 'aqua regia' treatment affect the surface composition of the Mo-rich phases differently than the Ni-rich matrix?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that aqua regia was used to remove the oxide layer after heat treatment, but it does not provide data or discussion on whether this treatment affects Mo-rich phases differently than the Ni-rich matrix.

answers.answer: The samples were treated with aqua regia to remove the oxide layer, but the differential effect on Mo-rich phases versus the Ni-rich matrix is not addressed in the provided text.
answers.material: Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 (with Mo addition)
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison of phase dissolution rates provided
evidence_spans: The alloy Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 exhibited a dendritic microstructure after the casting process.
Subsequent annealing for 50 h at 900 °C lead to a three-phase microstructure
Figure 1 a) shows the large (several 10 µm), randomly distributed Heusler type phase, with its characteristic needle-like shape and a volume-fraction of <5%.

source_evidence_spans: After heat treatment the rods cooled down to room temperature in the furnace. To remove the oxide layer the samples were initially sand-blasted and afterwards treated with aqua regia.
